title: Low-rank propagation for tridiagonalizable open quantum systems: near-linear scaling with system size
authors: Roman Ovsiannikov, Kurt Jacobs, Andrii G. Sotnikov, Denys I. Bondar
abstract: The quadratic growth of the density matrix with Hilbert-space dimension D is the central obstacle to simulating large open quantum systems. We introduce a deterministic algorithm that eliminates it for Lindblad dynamics whose Hamiltonian consists of a time-dependent diagonal part plus terms that are tridiagonal after reordering the basis. The state is a low-rank ensemble of vectors, propagated by tridiagonal split-operator steps and ensemble rank truncation of short-time Kraus branches, so that memory and cost per step are linear in D at fixed rank. For a driven nitrogen-vacancy-cavity model, rank 16 reproduces full density-matrix observables to relative error below $10^{-5}$, the method is up to two orders of magnitude faster than QuTiP already at $D \approx 500$, and its runtime scales nearly linearly.
summary: This paper presents a novel, deterministic algorithm to simulate large open quantum systems governed by the Lindblad equation. By exploiting the tridiagonal structure of the system Hamiltonian and employing ensemble rank truncation, the method achieves near-linear scaling with system size. This breakthrough significantly accelerates simulations for models like NV-cavity systems, making previously intractable dynamics accessible.
main_problem: The central obstacle in simulating large open quantum systems is the quadratic growth of the density matrix ($ho$) with the Hilbert-space dimension ($D$).
main_result: The authors introduce a deterministic algorithm that achieves memory and computational cost linear in $D$ for fixed low rank $R$, significantly accelerating simulations compared to existing tools like QuTiP.
method: The method combines exploiting the tridiagonal structure of the Hamiltonian for coherent evolution (using split-operator steps) with Ensemble Rank Truncation (ERT) for the dissipative Lindblad evolution.
model_or_system: The method is tested on open quantum systems governed by the Lindblad equation, specifically using a driven nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center coupled to a cavity.

important_parameters: The retained ensemble rank ($R$) is crucial; the method is most efficient when the system structure allows for tridiagonalization.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the Hamiltonian and collapse operators can be ordered such that they are diagonal or tridiagonal. The efficiency relies on the ability to truncate the ensemble rank $R$ while maintaining accuracy.
paper_structure: The paper develops a general ERT propagation algorithm for open systems with sparse structure, detailing the split-operator approach for unitary evolution and the Gram matrix compression for the dissipative map.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, scalable numerical tool for simulating complex open quantum dynamics in systems like cavity QED or NV centers, overcoming the exponential scaling bottleneck inherent in density matrix methods.
